analysis.title: GS Munaim - 1800 For A Night At Legoland - 14 Nov 2026
key_insights: Inflation has dominated economic and political discussion. The author says cost-of-living was the top voter issue in the recent US mid-term elections, and that recent CPI prints now confirm what anecdotes had shown.

Anecdotal evidence points to resilient consumer demand despite high prices. The on-property Legoland hotel was almost sold out at $1800 a night, and a Christmas flight to Asia was sold out, with flights a day earlier almost 40% more expensive.
The author says 50bp Fed hikes have entered the dialog at a time when anxiety about the economy is 'reaching a fever pitch'.

GS research added a third 25bp hike in March 2027 to its forecast after the October CPI report surprised meaningfully to the upside across several categories. This is the third month of worse inflation news.

GS continues to expect a second 25bp hike in December. A third hike could come in January, but March is judged more likely because November and December inflation reports are expected to be softer, followed by larger start-of-year price increases in January.

Post-midterm price action did not carry much into FX because the trade was not obvious and positioning was light. The surprise US CPI number got FX moving, but flows were muted by the mid-week US holiday, low conviction and light positioning.
Where flows occurred, they were USD buying spread across various currencies.

In USDJPY, positioning in recent weeks had built up in the long JPY trade, and the latest move washed some of it out. For clients who like long JPY as a fundamental position or AI equity hedge, the desk saw it as a chance to add, mainly via options. There was also short-dated protection buying against this core view.

GS FX Research argues FX vol is worth owning under policy divergence and/or growth shocks. The risk of growth shocks has diminished over the past week, while policy divergence has come to the fore as US data exceptionalism grows.
GS FX Research likes owning USD calls against CHF (over yearend) and against EUR (into the French election). The EUR leg is also described as a hedge against Middle East reescalation.

The GS Macro Weekend Webcast covers post-midterm politics and the AI build-out (data centre scrutiny and moratorium risk), prospects for a Middle East settlement, the US inflation trajectory and USD outlook, AI infrastructure and hyperscaler funding gaps, and whether the recent semiconductor de-grossing has created opportunities in semis and memory.

tension_points.bull_case: Policy divergence is coming to the fore as US data exceptionalism grows and the US economy looks capable of withstanding higher rates, which supports USD calls against CHF and EUR.
tension_points.bear_case: Positioning and conviction were low, and flows did not fully back up the CPI-driven USD moves. A Middle East reescalation is cited as a risk, and the EUR leg is positioned as a hedge for it.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A return of growth shocks, which the report says have diminished over the past week.
